mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a strengthening manufacturing sector, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises above 0.5% for four months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration above 100,000 new jobs for three consecutive months, accompanied by a concurrent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5%, signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 100000 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 3.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1,000,000 units for five consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.4% coincident with a federal funds rate below 1.5% signals an unexpected inflation shock under accommodative policy, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers a negative S&P 500 response over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 0.3% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by > 0.3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for four consecutive months signals a deep labor slack, which depresses consumer spending and corporate investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
